svg.title: Bus seat booking system: complete corrected design
svg.desc: Architecture, state machines, normal and failure flows, race conditions, double booking protection, database schema and API design.
svg.text: Bus seat booking system (RedBus style): corrected end-to-end design
Single source of truth in Inventory Postgres. Conditional updates prevent double booking. Redis is only a cache. Late payments are refunded if the seat is gone.

g.text: Purple: services. Teal: source of truth. Gray dashed: cache or external.

svg.text: Owns order and payment state, runs
Seat map from replica and Redis.
May be stale: the hold is the check.
Safe to lose at any time.
AVAILABLE to HELD: seat is AVAILABLE, or HELD with an expired hold.
HELD to BOOKED: seat is HELD by this same order (held_by_order match).
HELD to AVAILABLE: released by the holder, or swept after expiry.
Zero rows updated means another request won. Caller takes its fallback.
3. Normal flow: user books a seat
User selects seats. Client calls POST /v1/orders with Idempotency-Key.
Order service inserts the order as CREATED in the Orders DB.
Order service calls Inventory POST /internal/v1/holds. One transaction
holds all seats or none. Any seat already taken returns 409.
Order becomes SEAT_HELD, hold_expires_at = now + 10 min. Client gets
orderId and the expiry time to show a countdown.
User pays via POST /v1/orders/{id}/payments. Payment service creates
a PSP intent. Order becomes PAYMENT_PENDING.
PSP webhook hits Payment service. It dedupes by PSP event id and emits
Order service calls Inventory confirm: seat HELD to BOOKED, order to
CONFIRMED. Ticket is sent to the user by SMS and email.
Payment success is driven by the PSP webhook, not by the browser
redirect, because users close tabs. Confirm is idempotent.
Hold TTL: 10 minutes from the hold, shown to the user as a countdown.
Hold sweeper: every 30 seconds, batches with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
Order sweeper: waits a 60 s grace window, checks PSP status, then expires.
Outbox relay: retries with backoff until the call is acknowledged.
4. Failure flows and who clears seats
Webhook reports payment.failed. Order becomes FAILED and a RELEASE
row goes to the outbox. The relay calls Inventory release, retried
until acknowledged. Seat returns to AVAILABLE.
Nothing happens until the hold expires. Then lazy expiry or the hold
sweeper frees the seat and the Order sweeper marks the order EXPIRED.
On payment.succeeded for an EXPIRED order, the Order service asks
Inventory to confirm. If the seat is still held by this order or is
free, confirm succeeds and the order becomes CONFIRMED. If someone
took it, the order becomes REFUNDED and Payment service refunds.
Never keep the money without giving a seat.
1. Lazy expiry: the hold query treats an expired HELD seat as free.
2. Explicit release by Order service on failure or cancel (outbox).
3. Hold sweeper (Inventory): every 30 s, expired HELD to AVAILABLE,
in batches, then emits seat.released for cache refresh.
4. Order sweeper (Orders): expires stale orders, retries releases.
Correctness never depends on a sweeper being on time (see rule 1).
Webhooks are deduped by webhook_events.psp_event_id (primary key).
Create order is deduped by UNIQUE (user_id, idempotency_key).
Confirm and release check current state, so retries are harmless.
Two users grab the same seat
The hold is one atomic statement. Row locking serializes callers:
-- 1 row affected = you hold it; 0 rows = taken (409)
First caller: 1 row affected, wins. Second caller then sees HELD with
a future expiry: 0 rows affected, gets 409. No Redis needed.
Both are conditional updates on one row, so Postgres orders them.
Release needs held_by_order = old order; confirm needs the confirming
order or a free seat. First commit wins; the loser takes its fallback
Double booking: five layers of protection
1. Conditional UPDATE on status is the primary guard.
2. Confirm needs held_by_order = this order; stale confirms fail.
3. seat_bookings has UNIQUE (trip_id, seat_no) as a hard backstop.
4. Multi-seat holds run in one transaction: all seats or none.
5. Redis loss is harmless; Redis is never used for correctness.
Optional SET NX EX 600 can reject obviously taken seats fast, but a
Postgres check always follows. A wrong Redis answer breaks nothing.
trip_id, seat_no, order_id UUID, booked_at -- backstop
user_id UUID, trip_id TEXT, amount_paise INT
Seat map from Search (replica + cache). May be slightly stale.
Returns {paymentId, redirectUrl}. 410 if the hold has expired.
Order status and seat details (client polls).
User cancels. Triggers release through the outbox.
Signature verified, deduped by PSP event id, answers 200 fast.
{tripId, seatNos[], orderId, ttlSeconds}. All seats or none.
HELD to BOOKED if held_by_order matches. Idempotent.
Release if still held by this order. Idempotent.
Assumption: one Postgres primary per region; at higher scale shard the Inventory DB by trip_id so all seats of a trip stay in one transaction. Cassandra is removed.
